questions.question: The upstream speed of a boat is 18 km/hr. The speed of stream is 2 km/hr. What is the speed of the boat in downstream?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between downstream speed and upstream speed is always twice the speed of the stream.

⇒ Downstream Speed = Upstream Speed + 2 × Speed of Stream

⇒ Downstream Speed = 18 + 2 × 2

⇒ Downstream Speed = 18 + 4 = 22 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 22 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Upstream speed = 18 km/hr

Speed of stream = 2 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Upstream speed = Speed of boat in still water − Speed of stream

Downstream speed = Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bbe670d536cc8887916aa86d1f5b385a93b7a986c9cbc7aaafd066d585aa7578.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of the boat in still water be u and the speed of the stream be v.

⇒ u − v = 18

⇒ u − 2 = 18

⇒ u = 18 + 2

⇒ u = 20 km/hr

⇒ Downstream speed = u + v

⇒ Downstream speed = 20 + 2 = 22 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 22 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed in Still Water

It is the average of the downstream and upstream speeds: u = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Speed of Stream

It is half of the difference between the downstream and upstream speeds: v = (Downstream Speed − Upstream Speed) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed Concept

When moving with the flow of the stream, speeds add up (u + v). When moving against the flow, the effective speed is the difference (u − v).
</p

questions.question: ΔABC is equilateral triangle with side 12 cm. CD is the bisector of ∠C which meets AB at D and E is the mid-point of CD. What is the length of BE?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an equilateral triangle, altitude = (√3 ÷ 2) × side = (√3 ÷ 2) × 12 = 6√3 cm.

Angle bisector CD is also the altitude and median, making BD = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm.

Since E is the midpoint of CD, DE = 6√3 ÷ 2 = 3√3 cm.

Using Pythagoras theorem in right ΔBDE: BE = √(BD² + DE²) = √(6² + (3√3)²).

BE = √(36 + 27) = √63 = 3√7 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 3√7 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Side of equilateral ΔABC = 12 cm.

CD is the bisector of ∠C meeting AB at D, and E is the mid-point of CD.

**Formula Used:**

Altitude of equilateral triangle = (√3 ÷ 2) × side

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

 

 
• 
 
•

**Calculations:**

In an equilateral triangle, the angle bisector is also the median and altitude to the opposite side.

⇒ ΔCDB is a right-angled triangle at D.

⇒ BD = AB ÷ 2 = 12 ÷ 2 = 6 cm

⇒ CD = (√3 ÷ 2) × 12 = 6√3 cm

Since E is the midpoint of CD:

⇒ DE = CD ÷ 2 = 6√3 ÷ 2 = 3√3 cm

Now, applying Pythagoras theorem in right-angled ΔEDB:

⇒ BE² = BD² + DE²

⇒ BE² = 6² + (3√3)²

⇒ BE² = 36 + 27 = 63

⇒ BE = √63 = √(9 × 7) = 3√7 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 3√7 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equilateral Triangle Properties

In an equilateral triangle, all three sides are equal, and each angle is 60°. The altitude, median, angle bisector, and perpendicular bisector drawn from any vertex are exactly the same line.

Altitude Formula

The length of an altitude (h) in an equilateral triangle of side 'a' is given by the formula h = (√3 ÷ 2) × a.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: H² = P² + B².
</p

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume convenient values for the variables, let x = 2 and y = 1.

Numerator = (2² + 1²)(2 − 1) − (2 − 1)³ = 5 × 1 − 1 = 4

Denominator = 2² × 1 − 2 × 1² = 4 − 2 = 2

Expression value = Numerator ÷ Denominator = 4 ÷ 2 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: [(x² + y²)(x − y) − (x − y)³] / (x²y − xy²)

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ [(x² + y²)(x − y) − (x − y)³] / (x²y − xy²)

Taking (x − y) common from the numerator and xy from the denominator:

⇒ {(x − y)[(x² + y²) − (x − y)²]} / [xy(x − y)]

⇒ [(x² + y²) − (x − y)²] / xy

Expanding the (x − y)² term:

⇒ [(x² + y²) − (x² + y² − 2xy)] / xy

⇒ (x² + y² − x² − y² + 2xy) / xy

⇒ 2xy / xy

⇒ 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Standard formulas like (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab are fundamental for quickly expanding and simplifying algebraic expressions.

Value Substitution Method

When the options are numerical constants independent of variables, substituting small, distinct integers (like 1, 2) is often the fastest way to deduce the answer. Always ensure the chosen values do not make the denominator zero.
</p

questions.question: The monthly income of a person was Rs. 12,000 and his monthly expenditure was Rs. 10,000. In the next year, his income increased by 12% and his expenditure by 5%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Income : Expenditure : Savings = 12000 : 10000 : 2000 ⇒ 6 : 5 : 1.

Applying the percentage change weighted rule: (Income Ratio × % Change) = (Expenditure Ratio × % Change) + (Savings Ratio × S%)

⇒ 6 × 12 = (5 × 5) + (1 × S)

⇒ 72 = 25 + S ⇒ S = 47%

**∴ The correct answer is 47%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3c36501ea4daa12f8f67264eb492d278ce5b4a81636b45dbebebaaaa70c05bb.png] 

**Given:**

Initial Income = ₹12,000

Initial Expenditure = ₹10,000

**Formula Used:**

Savings = Income − Expenditure

Percentage Increase = (Increase in value ÷ Original value) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Savings = ₹12,000 − ₹10,000 = ₹2,000

⇒ New Income = ₹12,000 + (12% of 12,000) = 12,000 + 1,440 = ₹13,440

⇒ New Expenditure = ₹10,000 + (5% of 10,000) = 10,000 + 500 = ₹10,500

⇒ New Savings = ₹13,440 − ₹10,500 = ₹2,940

⇒ Increase in Savings = ₹2,940 − ₹2,000 = ₹940

⇒ Percentage Increase = (940 ÷ 2000) × 100 = 47%

**∴ The correct answer is 47%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income and Expenditure Relationship

Income is the sum of Expenditure and Savings (Income = Expenditure + Savings). Any change in overall income must be balanced by an equivalent combined change in expenditure and savings.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage Change = (Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value × 100. It measures the relative increase or decrease of an entity over a given time period.

Weighted Ratio Trick

When a total amount is divided into distinct parts, the overall percentage change is the weighted average of the individual changes: Total Ratio × %ΔTotal = Part1 Ratio × %ΔPart1 + Part2 Ratio × %ΔPart2.
</p

questions.question: For all real values of x, the minimum value of (1 - x + x²)/(1 + x + x²) is equal to
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ For any rational algebraic expression of the form (x² − ax + b) / (x² + ax + b), the maximum and minimum values always occur at x = ±√b. Here, a = 1 and b = 1. So, the extreme values occur at x = ±√1 = ±1. At x = 1, expression value = (1 − 1 + 1) / (1 + 1 + 1) = 1/3 At x = −1, expression value = (1 + 1 + 1) / (1 − 1 + 1) = 3/1 = 3 Thus, the minimum value is 1/3. **∴ The correct answer is 1/3.**

questions.question: The value of ((253)³ + (247)³)/(25.3 times 25.3 - 624.91 + 24.7 times 24.7) is 50 x K³, Find the value of K?

Balvendra offers two successive discounts of 9% and 4% first and then he also provides a cash discount of Rs.268 on the sale of a CCTV camera. If the marked price of the CCTV camera is Rs.5,000, what is the final price of the CCTV camera for a customer?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Calculate successive discounts using direct multiplying factors for efficiency:

Price after 9% and 4% discount = MP × 0.91 × 0.96

⇒ Price = 5000 × 0.91 × 0.96 = 4550 × 0.96 = 4368

Subtracting the final cash discount of Rs.268:

Final Price = 4368 − 268 = 4100

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.4,100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of CCTV = Rs. 5000

Successive discounts = 9% and 4%

Additional cash discount = Rs. 268

**Formula Used:**

Final Price = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100) − Cash Discount

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/446089da46bd56145469a47a4f46e0f349388036dda58c1b7c3eb06e83d3cadf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 1st discount (9%) = 5000 − (5000 × 9/100) = 5000 − 450 = Rs. 4550

⇒ Price after 2nd discount (4%) = 4550 − (4550 × 4/100) = 4550 − 182 = Rs. 4368

⇒ Final Price = Rs. 4368 − Rs. 268 (cash discount)

⇒ Final Price = Rs. 4100

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.4,100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When multiple discounts are given sequentially on the continuously reduced value, they are known as successive discounts. The equivalent single discount percentage for two successive discounts d₁ and d₂ is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁×d₂/100)%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

A discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The amount the customer finally pays is the Selling Price (SP), given by SP = MP − Discount Amount.

Cash Discount

A cash discount is an outright fixed monetary reduction subtracted directly from the total bill, unlike percentage discounts which scale proportionately with the base amount.
</p

questions.question: Rashi can finish a work alone in 10 hours, Gopi alone in 8 hours and Manju alone in 12 hours. How long will they take if they worked together?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(10, 8, 12) = 120 units

Combined efficiency = (120 ÷ 10) + (120 ÷ 8) + (120 ÷ 12) = 12 + 15 + 10 = 37 units/hour

Time taken together = Total work ÷ Combined efficiency = 120 ÷ 37 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3 ⁹/₃₇ hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rashi can finish the work in 10 hours.

Gopi can finish the work in 8 hours.

Manju can finish the work in 12 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of all individual times

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Total Time = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

 
 

 **Person**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Rashi
 10
 120
 12
 
 

 Gopi
 8
 15
 
 

 Manju
 12
 10
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of Rashi, Gopi and Manju = 12 + 15 + 10 = 37 units/hour

⇒ Time taken to complete the work together = 120 ÷ 37

⇒ Time = 3 ⁹/₃₇ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3 ⁹/₃₇ hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in proportion to the total work done by each person. If individuals work for the same number of days, the wages are divided in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The core concept is identical to Time and Work. An inlet pipe adds to the work (positive efficiency), while an outlet pipe or leak removes from the work (negative efficiency).

Alternate Day Work

When people work on alternate days, find the combined work completed in one full cycle (e.g., 2 days) and multiply by the maximum possible full cycles to reach near the total work.
</p

questions.question: An amount becomes double in 8 years on simple interest. In how many years would Rs. 25,000 become Rs. 1,00,000 with the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In Simple Interest, the interest earned is directly proportional to the time period.

Interest required for an amount to double = P (1 time the principal)

Time taken to earn interest equal to the principal = 8 years.

New Principal = 25,000 and New Amount = 1,00,000 ⇒ Interest required = 75,000.

Since 75,000 is 3 times the principal (25,000), time required = 3 × 8 = 24 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

An amount becomes double in 8 years.

New Principal (P₂) = 25,000 and New Amount (A₂) = 1,00,000.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

 
 
• 
 
 P
 
 2P
 

 8 years
 SI = P

 
 
• 

 
 
• 
 
 25,000
 
 1,00,000
 

 T years
 SI = 75,000 (3P)
 
 
 Since SI is 3 times the Principal, Time = 3 × 8 = 24 years

**Calculations:**

Let the original principal be P.

⇒ Amount = 2P

⇒ SI₁ = 2P − P = P

⇒ P = (P × R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 8 = 12.5%

For the second case:

⇒ P₂ = 25,000 and A₂ = 1,00,000

⇒ SI₂ = 1,00,000 − 25,000 = 75,000

⇒ 75,000 = (25,000 × 12.5 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 75,000 = 250 × 12.5 × T

⇒ 75,000 = 3125 × T

⇒ T = 75,000 ÷ 3125 = 24 years

**∴ The correct answer is 24 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is the principal, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period.

Amount Formula

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

Shortcut for Multiples

If a sum becomes 'n' times in 'T' years at simple interest, then the Rate of Interest R = ((n − 1) × 100) ÷ T %.
</p

questions.question: A can finish a work in 15 days, B can finish the same work in 25 days. They work together for 5 days. The rest of the work is finished by A and C in 4 days. Then C alone can finish the work in:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 15 and 25 = 75 units.

Efficiency of A = 75 ÷ 15 = 5, Efficiency of B = 75 ÷ 25 = 3.

Work done by A and B in 5 days = 5 × (5 + 3) = 40 units.

Remaining work = 75 − 40 = 35 units.

Combined efficiency of A and C = 35 ÷ 4 = 8.75 units/day.

Efficiency of C = 8.75 − 5 = 3.75. Time taken by C = 75 ÷ 3.75 = 20 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 15 days

Time taken by B to complete the work = 25 days

A and B work together for 5 days.

Remaining work is completed by A and C in 4 days.

**Calculations:**

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 15
 75
 5
 
 

 B
 25
 3
 
 

⇒ Work completed by A and B in 5 days = 5 × (5 + 3) = 40 units

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Completed work = 75 − 40 = 35 units

⇒ A and C complete this remaining work in 4 days.

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and C = Remaining work ÷ Time = 35 ÷ 4 = 35/4 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = Combined efficiency of (A + C) − Efficiency of A

⇒ Efficiency of C = 35/4 − 5 = (35 − 20) / 4 = 15/4 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total work ÷ Efficiency of C = 75 ÷ (15/4) = 75 × (4/15) = 20 days

**∴ The correct answer is 20 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

Total Work is typically taken as the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual time periods. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

The efficiency of a person is inversely proportional to the time taken by them to complete a piece of work. If the ratio of time taken is a:b, their efficiency ratio will be b:a.

Chain Rule (Group Work)

If M₁ men can do W₁ work in D₁ days working H₁ hours per day, and M₂ men can do W₂ work in D₂ days working H₂ hours per day, then (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂.
</p

questions.question: The sides ST and TR and the median SU of the Δ STR are equal to the sides MN and NJ and the median MV of the Δ MNJ, respectively. If ∠TSU = 46°, ∠NMJ = 79°and ∠MVN = 88°, what is the degree measure of = (7)/(11)∠SRT?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since U and V are midpoints of TR and NJ, TR = NJ ⇒ TU = NV.

By SSS congruence, ΔSTU ≅ ΔMNV (ST = MN, SU = MV, TU = NV).

This gives ∠NMV = ∠TSU = 46° and ∠MNJ = 180° − (46° + 88°) = 46°.

In ΔMNJ, ∠MJN = 180° − (∠MNJ + ∠NMJ) = 180° − (46° + 79°) = 55°.

By SAS congruence, ΔSTR ≅ ΔMNJ ⇒ ∠SRT = ∠MJN = 55°.

Required measure = 7/11 × 55° = 35°.

**∴ The correct answer is 35°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Sides ST = MN

⇒ Side TR = NJ

⇒ Median SU = Median MV

⇒ ∠TSU = 46°, ∠NMJ = 79°, and ∠MVN = 88°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ SSS Congruence Rule: If three sides are equal, the triangles are congruent.

⇒ SAS Congruence Rule: If two sides and the included angle are equal, the triangles are congruent.

 
 
• S T R U 46° 
 
• M N J V 79° 88° 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• ∴ ∠SRT = 55° 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since SU and MV are medians, U and V divide the bases TR and NJ into equal halves.

⇒ TR = NJ ⇒ TR/2 = NJ/2 ⇒ TU = NV

⇒ Consider ΔSTU and ΔMNV: ST = MN, SU = MV, and TU = NV.

⇒ By SSS congruence, ΔSTU ≅ ΔMNV.

⇒ This implies corresponding angles are equal: ∠NMV = ∠TSU = 46°, and ∠SUT = ∠MVN = 88°.

⇒ In ΔMNV, using angle sum property: ∠MNV = 180° − (46° + 88°) = 46°.

⇒ Angle ∠MNJ is the same as ∠MNV, hence ∠MNJ = 46°.

⇒ In the full ΔMNJ, angle sum property gives: ∠MJN = 180° − (∠MNJ + ∠NMJ) = 180° − (46° + 79°) = 55°.

⇒ Now compare ΔSTR and ΔMNJ: ST = MN, TR = NJ, and the included angles ∠STR = ∠MNJ (since ΔSTU ≅ ΔMNV).

⇒ By SAS congruence, ΔSTR ≅ ΔMNJ.

⇒ Therefore, corresponding angles are equal: ∠SRT = ∠MJN = 55°.

⇒ Required value = 7/11 × ∠SRT = 7/11 × 55° = 35°.

**∴ The correct answer is 35°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Congruence of Triangles (SSS and SAS)

Two triangles are identically congruent if all three corresponding sides are equal (SSS), or if two sides and the included angle are equal (SAS). Congruent triangles have exactly the same size and shape.

Median of a Triangle

A line segment joining a vertex to the exact midpoint of the opposite side. It cleanly divides the opposite side into two identical half-segments.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles in any planar triangle always equals 180°. This is a fundamental rule used repeatedly to find unknown missing angles.

questions.question: If 3⁽²p⁺⁴⁾ = 6561 , then find the value of (p + 1)⁴
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert 6561 into a power of 3: 6561 = 3⁸.

Equating the exponents of base 3: 2p + 4 = 8 ⇒ 2p = 4 ⇒ p = 2.

Substitute p = 2 to find the required expression: (p + 1)⁴ = (2 + 1)⁴ = 3⁴ = 81.

**∴ The correct answer is 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

3⁽²p⁺⁴⁾ = 6561

**Formula Used:**

If am = aⁿ for any base a > 1, then m = n.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3⁽²p⁺⁴⁾ = 6561

Factorizing 6561 gives:

⇒ 3⁽²p⁺⁴⁾ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3

⇒ 3⁽²p⁺⁴⁾ = 3⁸

Since the bases are the same, we can safely equate the exponents:

⇒ 2p + 4 = 8

⇒ 2p = 8 − 4

⇒ 2p = 4

⇒ p = 2

Now, substitute the value of p into the required expression (p + 1)⁴:

⇒ (2 + 1)⁴

⇒ 3⁴

⇒ 81

**∴ The correct answer is 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Law of Exponents (Multiplication & Division)

When multiplying terms with the same base, add their exponents: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ. When dividing, subtract them: am ÷ aⁿ = am−ⁿ.

Power of a Power Rule

When raising a power to another power, multiply the exponents: (am)ⁿ = am×ⁿ.

Zero and Negative Exponents

Any non-zero base to the power of 0 is 1: a⁰ = 1. A negative exponent denotes the reciprocal of the base raised to the positive power: a−ⁿ = 1 ÷ aⁿ.
</p

questions.question:
In parallelogram ABCD, if two points P and Q are taken on diagonal BD such that DP = BQ, which of the following statement (s) is/are correct?

(a) ΔAPD ≅ ΔCQB

(b) AP = CQ 

(c) AQ = CP
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the symmetry of a parallelogram, its diagonals bisect each other exactly at the center.

Since DP = BQ, points P and Q are equidistant from the center and lie on the same diagonal.

This symmetric placement ensures that the quadrilateral APCQ formed inside is also a parallelogram.

Therefore, opposite sides must be equal, giving AP = CQ and AQ = CP.

Additionally, the exact reflection across the center makes ΔAPD and ΔCQB perfectly congruent.

**∴ The correct answer is (a), (b) and (c).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ ABCD is a parallelogram.

⇒ Points P and Q are on diagonal BD such that DP = BQ.

**To check statements (a) and (b):**

⇒ In ΔAPD and ΔCQB,

⇒ AD = CB (Opposite sides of a parallelogram)

⇒ DP = BQ (Given data)

⇒ ∠ADP = ∠CBQ (Alternate interior angles, since AD || BC and BD is a transversal)

⇒ By SAS congruence criterion, ΔAPD ≅ ΔCQB.

⇒ This implies that statement (a) is correct.

⇒ By CPCT rule, corresponding parts of congruent triangles are exactly equal.

⇒ AP = CQ

⇒ This implies that statement (b) is correct.

**To check statement (c):**

⇒ Similarly, in ΔAQB and ΔCPD,

⇒ AB = CD (Opposite sides of a parallelogram)

⇒ BQ = DP (Given data)

⇒ ∠ABQ = ∠CDP (Alternate interior angles, since AB || CD and BD is a transversal)

⇒ By SAS congruence criterion, ΔAQB ≅ ΔCPD.

⇒ By CPCT rule, AQ = CP

⇒ This implies that statement (c) is also correct.

**∴ The correct answer is (a), (b) and (c).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Parallelogram

Opposite sides are mutually equal and parallel. Opposite angles are equal, and the diagonals bisect each other precisely at the center point of symmetry.

SAS Congruence Criterion

If two sides and the included angle of one triangle are found to be perfectly equal to the corresponding elements of another triangle, then the two triangles are defined as congruent.

CPCT Rule

The rule stands for 'Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles'. Whenever two triangles are established as congruent, all their related matching sides and angles naturally become equal.
</p

questions.question: A person had to reach a place, which was at a distance of 80 km in 7 hours. The distance was covered partially by foot at a speed of 8 km/h and the remaining by bicycle at a speed of 16 km/h. What was the distance covered by foot?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Shift Method:

If the entire 7 hours were covered by foot at 8 km/h, the distance would be 7 × 8 = 56 km.

Remaining distance to cover = 80 − 56 = 24 km.

Extra speed of bicycle over foot = 16 − 8 = 8 km/h.

Time spent on bicycle = 24 ÷ 8 = 3 hours, so time on foot = 7 − 3 = 4 hours.

Distance covered by foot = 4 hours × 8 km/h = 32 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 32 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 80 km

Total time = 7 hours

Speed on foot = 8 km/h

Speed on bicycle = 16 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a93be26f1545de74839204826c327ca98859622cbbfe56dfd278074ab0bf970b.png] 

**Calculation:**

Let the time travelled on foot be t hours.

⇒ Time travelled on bicycle = (7 − t) hours

Total distance = Distance on foot + Distance on bicycle

⇒ 8 × t + 16 × (7 − t) = 80

⇒ 8t + 112 − 16t = 80

⇒ 8t = 32

⇒ t = 4 hours

⇒ Distance covered by foot = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance covered by foot = 8 × 4 = 32 km

**∴ The correct answer is 32 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. When equal distances are covered at speeds a and b, the average speed becomes 2ab ÷ (a + b).

Alligation on Speed

When the rule of alligation is applied to the speeds of two parts of a journey, the resulting ratio gives the ratio of the time taken for each part, not the distance.

Relative Speed

If two objects are moving in the same direction, relative speed = |a − b|. If they are moving in opposite directions, relative speed = (a + b).
</p

questions.question: Train ‘A’ requires 15 seconds to cross train ‘B’ of length 300 m moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 36 km/h. Further, train ‘A’ requires 30 seconds to cross a 500 m long stationary train ‘C’. Find the length (in m) of train ‘A’.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of train B = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s.

For Train A to cross Train B, relative speed = Speed to cross stationary C + Speed of B.

⇒ (LA + 300) ÷ 15 = (LA + 500) ÷ 30 + 10

⇒ 2LA + 600 = LA + 500 + 300

⇒ LA = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of train B = 300 m

Speed of train B = 36 km/h = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

Length of stationary train C = 500 m

Time to cross B = 15 s, Time to cross C = 30 s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = VA + VB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/769276248a78aa7449ab538025ee5c0e35cc38fac6df147a92bbfaa750d86c87.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the length of train A be LA and its speed be VA.

⇒ Time taken to cross train B = (LA + 300) ÷ (VA + 10) = 15

⇒ VA + 10 = (LA + 300) ÷ 15 --- (1)

⇒ Time taken to cross stationary train C = (LA + 500) ÷ VA = 30

⇒ VA = (LA + 500) ÷ 30 --- (2)

⇒ Substituting equation (2) into equation (1):

⇒ [(LA + 500) ÷ 30] + 10 = (LA + 300) ÷ 15

⇒ Multiplying by 30 on both sides:

⇒ LA + 500 + 300 = 2 × (LA + 300)

⇒ LA + 800 = 2LA + 600

⇒ LA = 800 − 600 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds (V₁ + V₂). For the same direction, it is the difference (V₁ − V₂).

Crossing Objects

When a train crosses an object with length (like a platform or another train), the total distance covered equals the sum of lengths (L₁ + L₂).

Speed Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
</p

questions.question: P can do a piece of work in 48 days and Q and do half of the same work in 30 days. If they both work together, in how many days can they complete three - eigth of the work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(48, 60) = 240 units.

Efficiency of P = 240 ÷ 48 = 5 units/day.

Efficiency of Q = 240 ÷ (30 × 2) = 4 units/day.

Target Work = 3/8 × 240 = 90 units.

Required Time = 90 ÷ (5 + 4) = 10 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete the work = 48 days.

Time taken by Q to complete half of the work = 30 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by Q to complete the full work = 30 × 2 = 60 days.

⇒ Combined efficiency of P and Q = 5 + 4 = 9 units/day.

⇒ Target work = 3/8 of 240 = 3/8 × 240 = 90 units.

⇒ Time taken by P and Q together = Target work ÷ Combined efficiency.

⇒ Time taken = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to Time & Work, where the total capacity acts as total work. Filling pipe efficiency is positive, while an emptying pipe (leak) efficiency is negative.

Work and Wages

Wages are strictly divided in the ratio of the total work done. If people work for the same number of days, the wage ratio is directly equal to their efficiency ratio.

Alternate Day Work

Calculate the work completed in one cycle (e.g., A works day 1, B works day 2). Find the maximum whole cycles that fit into the total work, then assign the remaining work to the first person.

questions.question: If (x - (1)/(x))² = 10 and x>0, then what is value of x³ - (1)/(x³) ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If (x − 1/x)² = a, and x − 1/x = √a (taking the positive root),

Then direct formula: x³ − 1/x³ = (a + 3)√a

Given a = 10, substitute directly into the shortcut:

x³ − 1/x³ = (10 + 3)√10

x³ − 1/x³ = 13√10

**∴ The correct answer is 13√10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(x − 1/x)² = 10

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b)

Which gives: a³ − b³ = (a − b)³ + 3ab(a − b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Taking the square root on both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (x − 1/x) = √10 (considering the positive value as per options)

⇒ We need to find the value of x³ − 1/x³

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = (x − 1/x)³ + 3 × x × (1/x) × (x − 1/x)

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = (√10)³ + 3 × 1 × (√10)

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 10√10 + 3√10

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 13√10

**∴ The correct answer is 13√10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2 and x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k.

Negative Sign Identities

If x − 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² + 2 and x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k.

Conversion Between Plus and Minus

(x + 1/x)² − (x − 1/x)² = 4. This is highly useful for deducing the value of one expression from the other.
</p

questions.question: If sec A + tan A = 5, then sec A - tan A ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The trigonometric terms (sec A − tan A) and (sec A + tan A) are exact reciprocals of each other.

sec A − tan A = 1 ÷ (sec A + tan A)

Given that sec A + tan A = 5

⇒ sec A − tan A = 1/5

**∴ The correct answer is 1/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

sec A + tan A = 5

**Formula Used:**

sec²A − tan²A = 1

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

**Calculations:**

⇒ sec²A − tan²A = 1

Using the algebraic difference of squares formula:

⇒ (sec A − tan A)(sec A + tan A) = 1

Substitute the given value of (sec A + tan A) = 5 in the above equation:

⇒ (sec A − tan A) × 5 = 1

⇒ sec A − tan A = 1/5

**∴ The correct answer is 1/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identity

sin²A + cos²A = 1, which represents the relation between sine and cosine functions.

Cosecant and Cotangent Property

cosec²A − cot²A = 1, which implies that cosec A − cot A is always the exact reciprocal of cosec A + cot A.

Reciprocal and Ratio Forms

sec A = 1 ÷ cos A and tan A = sin A ÷ cos A
</p

questions.question: The ratio of gold and copper in 60 grams of alloy is 2 ∶ 1. How much more copper should be added to make the ratio 1 ∶ 2?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio of Gold to Copper = 2 ∶ 1 (Total = 3 units = 60 Grams ⇒ 1 unit = 20 Grams)

Final Ratio of Gold to Copper = 1 ∶ 2

Since Gold remains unchanged, equate the Gold units by multiplying the final ratio by 2 ⇒ 2 ∶ 4

Increase in Copper = 4 − 1 = 3 units ⇒ Added Copper = 3 × 20 = 60 Grams.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 Grams.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total weight of initial alloy = 60 Grams

Initial ratio of Gold to Copper = 2 ∶ 1

Final ratio of Gold to Copper = 1 ∶ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b523351719fb513b3f3584e10277eef6c6d206013274e9d2dd8dd433d15a7bbf.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the initial weight of Gold be 2x and Copper be x.

⇒ Total initial weight = 2x + x = 60

⇒ 3x = 60 ⇒ x = 20 Grams

⇒ Initial quantity of Gold = 2 × 20 = 40 Grams

⇒ Initial quantity of Copper = 20 Grams

Let y Grams of pure copper be added to the mixture.

⇒ New quantity of Copper = (20 + y) Grams

Since the new ratio of Gold to Copper is 1 ∶ 2:

⇒ 40 / (20 + y) = 1 / 2

⇒ 20 + y = 80

⇒ y = 60 Grams

**∴ The correct answer is 60 Grams.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Element Concept

When only one component of a mixture is altered (added or removed), the absolute quantity of the other component remains unchanged. Equating the constant component's parts across the initial and final ratios provides the fastest way to solve mixture problems.

Rule of Alligation

Used to find the exact ratio in which two distinct mixtures must be mixed. Formula: (Quantity of cheaper ÷ Quantity of dearer) = (Price of dearer − Mean price) ÷ (Mean price − Price of cheaper).

Replacement Formula

If from a vessel containing x units of a pure liquid, y units are drawn out and replaced with water, and this process is repeated n times, the amount of pure liquid left = x × (1 − y/x)ⁿ.

questions.question: A sphere of radius 5 cm is dropped in a right circular cylindrical vessel partly filled with water. The radius of the cylindrical vessel is 10 cm. If the sphere is completely submerged in water, by how much will the level of water rise in the cylindrical vessel ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to Archimedes' principle, the volume of water displaced equals the volume of the submerged object.

Rise in water level (h) = Volume of sphere ÷ Base area of cylinder

⇒ h = [4/3 × π × (5)³] ÷ [π × (10)²]

⇒ h = (4/3 × 125) ÷ 100

⇒ h = 500 ÷ 300 = 5/3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5/3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d1081774052b08c7c6bd9bec33b06350ec067513bb85aaf5de588c203a656a81.png] 

**Given:**

Radius of the sphere (R) = 5 cm

Radius of the cylindrical vessel (r) = 10 cm

Let the level of water rise by 'h' cm.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = 4/3 × π × R³

Volume of a cylinder = π × r² × h

**Calculation:**

According to the principle of volume displacement, the volume of water displaced is equal to the volume of the completely submerged sphere.

⇒ Volume of water raised = Volume of the sphere

⇒ π × r² × h = 4/3 × π × R³

⇒ π × (10)² × h = 4/3 × π × (5)³

⇒ 100 × h = 4/3 × 125

⇒ h = 500 ÷ (3 × 100)

⇒ h = 5/3 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 5/3 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume of a right circular cylinder is given by V = π × r² × h, where r is the base radius and h is the height of the cylinder.

Volume of a Sphere

The volume of a sphere is given by V = 4/3 × π × r³, where r is the radius of the sphere.

Archimedes' Principle (Volume Displacement)

When a solid object is completely submerged in a liquid, it displaces a volume of liquid exactly equal to its own volume. Therefore, Volume of liquid displaced = Volume of submerged object.
</p

questions.question: The average weight of a team of 32 IT employees is 54 kg. If the weight of the manager is included, then the average increases by 1 kg. Find the weight of the manager. (In kg)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Manager's weight = Old Average + (New Total Persons × Increase in Average)

⇒ Manager's weight = 54 + (33 × 1)

⇒ Manager's weight = 54 + 33 = 87 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 87 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial average weight of 32 employees (A₁) = 54 kg

New average weight after adding the manager (A₂) = 54 + 1 = 55 kg

Total number of people now (N₂) = 32 + 1 = 33

 
 
 

 
 

 
 32 Employees
 Avg = 54 kg
 
 
• 
 + Manager

 
 33 People (Total)
 Avg = 55 kg
 (Increase = +1 kg)

 
 Manager's Weight = 54 + (33 × 1) = 87 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Weight = Average × Number of persons

Manager's Weight = New Total Weight − Old Total Weight

**Calculations:**

⇒ Old Total Weight = 32 × 54

⇒ Old Total Weight = 1728 kg

⇒ New Total Weight = 33 × 55

⇒ New Total Weight = 1815 kg

⇒ Manager's Weight = 1815 − 1728

⇒ Manager's Weight = 87 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 87 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exclusion in Averages

When a person leaves a group, the weight of the person leaving = Old Average − (Remaining members × Decrease in Average).

Replacement Method

When one person replaces another in a group, Weight of new person = Weight of removed person ± (Total members × Change in Average).

Weighted Average

Used to find the combined average of two distinct groups: Aw = (N₁A₁ + N₂A₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂).
</p

questions.question: A sum amounts to ₹37044 in 3 years at 5% p.a., interest being compounded yearly. If the same sum amounts to ₹x in 16 months at 12% p.a., when the interest is compounded 8-monthly, then the value of x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiplying factor for 5% over 3 years is (21/20)³ = 9261/8000.

Principal P = 37044 × (8000 ÷ 9261) = ₹32000.

For 16 months compounded 8-monthly: Rate = 12% × (8 ÷ 12) = 8% per cycle, and Cycles = 16 ÷ 8 = 2.

Amount x = 32000 × (108/100)² = 32000 × 1.1664 = 37324.80.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹37324.80.**

Fractional Year Compounding

When compounding happens n-monthly, the applicable rate per cycle becomes R × (n/12), and the number of cycles becomes Total Time (in months) ÷ n.

Compound Interest

CI is evaluated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest from preceding periods. The fundamental formula is A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ.

questions.question: A famous basketball league team is planning to paint the entire basketball shaped dummy whose radius is 7 m. A painter is hired who tells that 5.4 liters of paint will be used to paint the area of 36 m². How much paint (in l) is required? (round of to one decimal place) Take pi = frac{22}7
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Surface Area of spherical dummy = 4 × π × r²

⇒ Area = 4 × (22/7) × 7² = 616 m²

Amount of paint used per m² = 5.4 ÷ 36 = 0.15 l/m²

Total paint required = 616 × 0.15 = 92.4 l

**∴ The correct answer is 92.4 l.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the spherical dummy (r) = 7 m

Paint used for 36 m² area = 5.4 l

**Formula Used:**

Total Surface Area of a Sphere = 4 × π × r²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0169af09a5ac2f104bf0242d1e19a6f638afd2dfc4524b6cf325da22a3d06abd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Surface Area = 4 × (22/7) × 7 × 7

⇒ Total Surface Area = 4 × 22 × 7 = 616 m²

⇒ Paint required for 1 m² = 5.4 ÷ 36 = 0.15 l

⇒ Total paint required = Area × Paint per m²

⇒ Total paint required = 616 × 0.15 = 92.4 l

**∴ The correct answer is 92.4 l.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The volume of a full sphere is given by the formula V = (4/3) × π × r³.

Surface Area of a Hemisphere

A solid hemisphere has a Curved Surface Area = 2 × π × r² and a Total Surface Area = 3 × π × r².

Volume of a Hemisphere

The volume of a hemisphere is exactly half of a full sphere, given by V = (2/3) × π × r³.
